basis: First actual source-pixel observations in this fresh context; edition prose supplies medium and apparatus interpretation, not invented source details.

items.fact: One shared optical frame, not separate panels or a grid.
A nearly horizontal boundary crosses the frame; broken horizontal strokes fill the lower medium. These strokes depict water, not a ruled measurement lattice.
One dark source point below the boundary near the horizontal center, labelled S beneath it.
Straight rays fan upward from the common S location to ordered positions on the same boundary, on both sides of a central vertical ray.
Seven prominent non-grazing rays extend upward into the upper medium, including the central vertical ray. Two additional shallow outward branches occur close to the boundary, one on each side.
Branches from boundary contacts return downward within the lower medium; outer contacts have near-horizontal incident and reflected branches without a clearly separate upward continuation.
Visible arrowheads on upward and shallow upper branches point away from the boundary and S. Lower return arrows point away from their boundary contacts.
Visible ray stroke thickness differs. The edition explicitly identifies thicker rays with stronger light; no quantitative intensity scale appears in the pixels.
S is the only confidently readable source label. No visible angle values, units, normal labels, prism labels or apparatus vessel outline.

relationships.fact: Incident rays share S below the boundary and meet one shared surface.
Incident, transmitted and return branches are associated at boundary contacts, not independent unconnected strokes.
Upper directions progress from vertical centrally to shallow outward directions toward the sides.
Return branches remain below the surface and propagate away from surface contacts.

holds.fact: The densely superposed surface and near-S strokes do not establish an exact inventory of every faint incident/reflected branch, arrowhead or linewidth. No exact weak-ray count or quantitative strength is certified.
Existing source-detail RAW/SVG holds remain unchanged; a modern FIG verdict does not clear them.

items.fact: One continuous, ribbon-like bundle of multiple closely spaced strands, not an optical-prism panel.
The body rises into a large rounded loop with a clear central opening and returns to the lower horizontal region. Outer and inner contours both define the bend.
A short horizontal segment and a dark oblique, approximately rectangular end face occur at the lower left, with several short strand strokes near the face.
A longer lower horizontal segment reaches a dark approximately rectangular end face at the lower right, also showing dense strand strokes.
Both end regions belong to the same drawn bundle. Exact fiber number, identity and pixel-by-pixel endpoint matching are not readable from the scan.

No confidently readable labels, directional arrowheads, angle values or quantitative dimensions are present. Assigning Input at left and Output at right is an explanatory modern convention, not a visible source arrow.

relationships.fact: Two terminal faces are connected through a bent, looped bundle, with a hollow center rather than a filled disk.
Dense short lines at both ends indicate multiple fibers; the source does not identify a specific small modern strand count.
The instructional path is curved and continuous, not a straight-only replacement or a prism-based sharp corner.

holds.fact: Exact strand count, end-face pattern and precise over/under structure at the dense lower overlap are not established by these source pixels.
Existing source-detail RAW/SVG holds remain unchanged; exact fiber order is a current-edition clarification, not a newly resolved original-source detail.
